newsitem.title: UK: Court gunwoman returns to London crime scene.
newsitem.headline: Court gunwoman returns to London crime scene.

text.p: A woman who brandished what was thought to be a gun in London's High Court was arrested on Friday after returning to the scene of the crime, waving an imitation pistol.
She strode through the front entrance of the courts complex before being arrested by police, witnesses said.

The woman escaped on Thursday after waving the gun at judges and court staff during a hearing at the Royal Courts of Justice in central London. She vanished in a maze of corridors and rooms at back of the building and evaded armed police.
Police were trying to trace the woman, who was thought to have a grudge against judges, when she returned.
A security guard said: "The same woman came back into the courts, she was waving a gun as she tried to walk through the security gates.
"It was clearly an imitation weapon. Luckily we had a couple of police waiting here in case she tried anything and we recognised her straight away because of the gun.
"There was a bit of a scuffle and she was arrested and taken away. I couldn't believe my eyes when I realised what was happening."
In Thursay's incident, the woman stood up in the public gallery of Court 7 and brandished an imitation pistol and pointing it at three judges hearing the case.
She then shouted: "I have been assaulted and I have waited long enough. People will be shot unless my appeal is heard today. They have taken my children."
